title: HCP — Restrict Entry Purposes — payload
description: The request payload of the HCP 2.0-draft-3 Restrict purposes operation (HCP 4.2.6, 5.4; `PUT /v2/entries/{entryId}/purposes` in HCP 9.2, 9.4.10): a Management Client, acting for the Authorizing Principal, sets or removes the Authorizing Principal's narrowing of the purposes an entry may be disclosed for. HCP defines no schema for this operation; the members come from HCP 9.2 and 9.4.10. The outer document members (id, type, issuer, recipient, issuedAt, expiresAt, proof) are owned by the framework — SPEC §6.3.

entryId.description: HCP `entryId` (the `{entryId}` path parameter of HCP 9.2, 9.4.10): the entry's stable `id` (HCP 4.2), by which a Management Client names an entry (HCP 9.4.5).

permittedPurposes.description: HCP `permittedPurposes`: the entry's new `classification.permittedPurposes`, the purpose codes it may be disclosed for (HCP 4.2.6, 9.4.10). It can only narrow: a purpose it lists that `assertion.permittedPurposes` does not list has no effect (HCP 4.2.6). Null removes the Authorizing Principal's narrowing (HCP 9.4.10); HCP's own value, carried verbatim. The maxItems of 256 and the minItems of 1 are framework bounds, not HCP requirements: an empty list would permit no purpose, which HCP does not define.

expectedVersion.description: HCP `expectedVersion`: the `record.version` the Management Client showed the Authorizing Principal. Where it is not the entry's current version, the operation fails with version conflict and changes nothing (HCP 5.4, 5.5).

accessToken.description: The Management Client's HCP access token (HCP 9.3), carried unchanged. HCP's HTTP binding sends it as a Bearer token; this member carries it in the document. The provider validates it exactly as over HTTP and treats it as opaque. The maxLength is a framework bound, not an HCP requirement.

Response.title: HCP — Restrict Entry Purposes — response payload
Response.description: The entry, with its new `classification.permittedPurposes`, absent where the narrowing was removed (HCP 9.4.10). HCP's result body is the entry itself; the carriage wraps it in `entry`. Failures use trust-task-error, not this shape.

entry.description: The HCP result (HCP 9.4.10): the whole entry, as a Management Client receives it (HCP 7.4). Its `record.version` is unchanged: a change of `classification` creates no version (HCP 4.2.1).
